chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (mercy of God upon him) narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn 'Imran al-Ash'ari, from Ali ibn Isma'il and Ibrahim ibn Hashim both, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I asked him — meaning Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — 'Is there anything that exists today that was not in the Knowledge of Allah, the Mighty and High?' He (peace be upon him) replied: 'No, but it was in His Knowledge before He raised the Heavens and the Earth.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about whether God's knowledge includes everything before creation?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Mansur ibn Hazim queries Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the eternity of divine knowledge, specifically whether any created entity was previously unknown to Allah. The Imam affirms that God’s knowledge is eternal and comprehensive, existing prior to the creation of the heavens and the earth, thereby establishing the doctrine of *Ilm al-Ilahi* as an essential attribute of the Divine Essence rather than an acquired accident.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 6. Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (RA), on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn `Imran al-Ash`ari, on the authority of `Ali ibn Ismai`il and Ibrahim ibn Hashim both, on the authority of Safwan ibn Yahya, on the authority of Mansur ibn Hazim that

I asked Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS): “Is there anything that exists today that was not in the Knowledge of Allah, the Mighty and High?” He (AS) replied: “No, His Knowledge encompassed everything even before He raised the Heavens and the Earth.”
